title: The Race Before the Race: Inside the High-Stakes World of a T‑Mobile Innovator at the FORMULA 1 LAS VEGAS GRAND PRIX
summary: What does it take to keep an entire city-turned-racetrack connected? T‑Mobile’s Jason Schnellbacher takes us behind the scenes.
body_markdown:
Talking to[Jason Schnellbacher](https://www.linkedin.com/in/g-jason-schnellbacher-7863901/) about his role in some of the country’s biggest sporting events, you might be surprised by how calmly he discusses the enormous responsibility on his team’s shoulders.


“I have one of the coolest jobs at T‑Mobile,” he says.


A member of T‑Mobile’s Network Technology Strategy team, Schnellbacher helps bring some of the company’s most ambitious connectivity projects to life. And as he prepares for his[fourth Las Vegas Grand Prix](https://www.t-mobile.com/news/network/t-mobile-powers-new-ways-to-experience-the-formula-1-heineken-las-vegas-grand-prix-on-and-off-the-track) , he talks about one of his most complicated assignments yet with an easy smile.


Instead of connecting fans inside a traditional stadium venue, his team is helping support an entire city transformed into a racetrack, with hundreds of thousands of racegoers, television crews, vendors, event staff and first responders all relying on connectivity across The Strip.


“It’s high stress, high stakes,” Schnellbacher says. “As our CTO John Saw likes to say, there’s no safety net. This is for real.”


Perhaps his demeanor is fitting for a job where the ultimate measure of success is something nobody is supposed to notice.


> It's not innovation if we're not doing new stuff, right?
>
>
> Jason Schnellbacher, T‑Mobile Network Technology Strategy Team


A ticket scans on the first try. A fan video calls family back home to share the spectacle. A photographer sends an unforgettable image from the track to viewers halfway around the world. And as Formula 1 cars roar down The Strip at speeds approaching 210 mph,[countless connections](https://www.t-mobile.com/business/why-tmobile/customer-success-stories) work quietly behind the scenes to keep the experience moving.


And for Schnellbacher, that’s exactly the point.


“You don’t think about it, it just works.”


He’s helped bring T‑Mobile technology to major sporting events across the country and seems more energized than intimidated by the prospect of raising the bar again.


“It’s not innovation if we’re not doing new stuff, right?”


## The City Is the Circuit


Schnellbacher’s mission has always been about doing more than simply talking about 5G. He wants to show people what it can actually make possible. And few places offer a more dramatic proving ground than the Las Vegas Grand Prix.


For the inaugural race in 2023, and as the official 5G partner, T‑Mobile’s focus was on establishing the network infrastructure and supporting essential services, including ticketing and point-of-sale transactions.


“A lot of times you went to a major sporting event, your phone didn’t work,” he recounts.


But he says T‑Mobile’s Ultra Capacity 5G network, together with its[Advanced Network Solutions](https://www.t-mobile.com/business/industry-solutions/connected-vehicle-network/ultra-capacity-5g-at-f1-las-vegas) , has fundamentally changed what’s possible when enormous crowds converge in one place.


To prepare for the first race, T‑Mobile expanded network capacity across the circuit and surrounding city, adding permanent infrastructure and temporary mobile cell sites where crowds would gather. The goal was to ensure fans, vendors and event personnel could stay connected even as hundreds of thousands of people took to the Las Vegas streets.


> We are the leader in 5G and these are the proof points that make it exciting.
>
>
> Jason Schnellbacher, T‑Mobile's Network Technology Strategy Team


And the network continues to evolve. For 2026, T‑Mobile is increasing its deployed 5G spectrum, giving the network additional capacity to handle the demands of race weekend.


“Last year we were running 745 megahertz of spectrum,” he explains. “This year it’s 845 with the addition of a mmWave channel. To put that into perspective, if you were going to make a highway metaphor, that’s like more than 80 lanes. That is a lot of capacity!”


But building more capacity is only part of the challenge. As the partnership with Formula 1 has evolved, Schnellbacher and his team have also found new ways to use the network. Last year, that ambition led to an unusual request: helping deliver footage from a camera perched atop the 42-story Mandalay Bay Resort and Casino, overlooking the spectacle below. The difficulty was getting that live footage into the international broadcast from a vantage point higher than T‑Mobile’s nearby cell sites.


Schnellbacher and his team helped develop a solution that bonded 5G connectivity with Starlink,[using network slicing](https://www.t-mobile.com/business/business-internet/superbroadband) to support the transmission. The result was another camera angle delivered to a broadcast reaching viewers in 130 countries.


“Some of the new camera angles that we’re able to provide inside the broadcast … are really amazing and really only possible with T‑Mobile’s Ultra-Capacity 5G,” Schnellbacher says.


For viewers at home, it’s another spectacular shot of a city transformed into a racetrack. But behind that fleeting moment on screen is the kind of technological challenge Schnellbacher loves solving.


### Behind the Numbers: T‑Mobile at the Las Vegas Grand Prix


In Vegas, everything runs at full throttle — and the network has to keep up.


For the 2025 Las Vegas Grand Prix, T‑Mobile reinforced its existing network with five mobile cell sites, two temporary rooftop sites and more than **120 5G** radios delivering a combined **745 MHz** of spectrum. For 2026, T‑Mobile’s network design is expanding to **152 5G** radios.


But it’s not just about adding more equipment. T‑Mobile’s network uses multiple layers of Ultra Capacity 5G, combining different spectrum bands to handle enormous demand across the circuit. That includes powerful high-band millimeter wave (mmWave) technology at mobile cell sites and major seating areas, helping deliver extra capacity where fans need it most.


Added capacity helped support **233,000** peak concurrent users, **45,000** voice calls and **52** terabytes of data for weekend attendance of more than **[300,000](https://www.t-mobile.com/business/industry-solutions/connected-vehicle-network/ultra-capacity-5g-at-f1-las-vegas)** in 2025. As fans move from one part of the action to another, their phones seamlessly switch between cells, helping them stay connected wherever race weekend takes them.


T‑Mobile’s dedicated 5G network slice helped[keep concession payments moving](https://www.t-mobile.com/business/why-tmobile/customer-success-stories)) last year, supporting fast, reliable transactions at **300+** payment terminals so fans could spend less time in line and more time enjoying the action.


Up to **5x more** network resources for first responders — T‑Mobile’s[T-Priority](https://www.t-mobile.com/news/network/t-mobile-puts-5g-innovation-in-the-drivers-seat-at-lvgp)) helps Las Vegas police and emergency crews stay connected and coordinate responses, even as massive crowds put the network to the test.


## The Art of Staying One Step Ahead


Of course, ensuring everything works smoothly is hardly as simple as switching on a network and waiting for the crowds. Much of Schnellbacher’s job involves anticipating challenges long before anyone else and finding solutions to problems that might seem impossible at first glance.


It’s a mindset that’s helping shape preparations for 2026. During last year’s race, a radio supporting production in the T‑Mobile Zone at Sphere unexpectedly lost power. The team had another site available to activate, but the incident became another lesson in preparedness, prompting plans for additional safeguards this year, including ruggedized backup power supplies and improved generator monitoring designed to give engineers more advance warning of potential problems.


The approach borrows from lessons learned elsewhere in T‑Mobile’s network operations, including the practice of hardening sites against[hurricanes](https://www.t-mobile.com/news/archive/emergency-response) . Schnellbacher says the principle is similar, only on a smaller scale. For him, those real-world lessons are more than operational improvements. They’re evidence of what T‑Mobile’s technology can accomplish when it’s put to the test.


“We are the leader in 5G, and these are the proof points that make it exciting,” he says.


Some precautions aren’t even about keeping the show running. They’re about being ready if something far more serious happens by positioning mobile cell site strategically to provide backup connectivity should an emergency arise. Together with solutions such as[T-Priority](https://www.t-mobile.com/t-priority?gclsrc=aw.ds&&cmpid=TFB_PB_P_TFBSAFETPR_2380047392339_179197390488_794002468476&gad_source=1&gad_campaignid=22134730484&gbraid=0AAAAAD79WuVe2tx0vaU2YaQRIjld2Kzsy&gclid=CjwKCAjwuobXBhBXEiwAYUaIlbgyscYvhJjXVsNqLC7RiwkT_Rxv_lek8ApMWfm0-RYOX5iGDAryKRoC7PAQAvD_BwE) , which gives[eligible first responders](https://www.t-mobile.com/news/community/how-a-retired-police-captain-aims-to-enhance-first-responder-connectivity) the highest priority network access, the added safeguards underscore how preparation is also about helping protect the people who came to enjoy it.


And the implications extend beyond Formula 1. The innovations demonstrated in Las Vegas offer a glimpse of what’s possible for other venues, businesses and cities facing similarly complex connectivity demands. And Schnellbacher is quick to credit the larger T‑Mobile team and its partners for making these innovations possible. From developing backup power solutions to improving generator monitoring, he says it’s a collective effort that takes the expertise of many people working behind the scenes.


### Members Get More at the Grand Prix


The FORMULA 1 HEINEKEN LAS VEGAS GRAND PRIX roars into town Thursday, Nov. 19 through Saturday, Nov. 21, with the main event Saturday night. If you’re a[T‑Mobile member](https://www.t-mobile.com/dialed-in/tips-tricks/how-to-watch-f1-las-vegas-grand-prix) on a qualifying plan, you’ve got a few ways to upgrade your weekend:


**Skip the crowd at Club Magenta.** Members get exclusive access to the VIP lounge inside the T‑Mobile Zone at Sphere, complete with luxe seating, free charging and room for up to two guests.


**Save on the Plaza.** Unlock 25% off tickets at Grand Prix Plaza.


**Find it all in T-Life.** Your full list of race week benefits is waiting[in the app](https://www.t-mobile.com/apps) .


[Learn More](https://www.t-mobile.com/benefits/las-vegas-grand-prix)


## The Best Seat in the House


And the work is far from finished. As T‑Mobile prepares for the Las Vegas Grand Prix 2026, Schnellbacher and his team are already looking for new ways to push the experience further, from ambitious broadcast camera angles to additional public safety and operational capabilities.


For someone whose job revolves around imagining what’s possible, one of the biggest challenges these days is knowing when to stop innovating long enough to put those plans into action.


“I’m the guy who is always trying to come up with the new or the next thing, sometimes even down to the last minute,” he admits.


And for Schnellbacher, some of the most satisfying moments are remarkably simple. During last year’s race, with everything running smoothly, he found himself standing in the T‑Mobile Zone at Sphere, watching the action on a big screen.


“I was \[finally\] able to catch some racing,” he says with a sense of relief.


For someone who spends so much time helping make the technology behind the spectacle invisible, perhaps that’s the ultimate reward: getting to forget about it himself and simply enjoy the race.


Jason Schnellbacher and team staging at the 2025 FORMULA 1 HEINEKEN LAS VEGAS GRAND PRIX
